rule: A record generates no runtime functions, unlike macros that do (`defdelegate`, `defexception`), whose generated functions are call targets.
notes: call_type convention (SPEC gives no Elixir mapping; Elixir has no methods and the `macro` type is defined only for C/C++/ObjC and Rust `name!`): every local, imported and remote call is direct, a call through a value is callback. Operators and special forms (`|>`, `=`, `case`, `fn`, `%{}`, `__MODULE__`) are language constructs, not calls. Bare Kernel functions resolve to the auto-imported Kernel (Elixir decision: 'with one import known to export the name, that import is the target'): `Kernel.<name>`, medium. `defexception [:message]` generates `exception/1` and, because the struct has a :message field, `message/1` (Elixir's documented default). They are defined in the scan, so calls to them are high and both are nodes (C1: a definition that edges reach is listed in nodes). `defexception` itself is a declaration, like defstruct: no edge. `Exception.message/1` is the standard library: medium.
